text:
HYBE, the K-pop powerhouse behind BTS, is making a major push into Japan's entertainment industry, seeking control of a company behind some of the country's best-known pop acts, including girl groups Nogizaka46 and SKE48, in a deal that could reshape its presence in the world's second-largest recorded music market.
HYBE Japan, the Korean entertainment company's Japanese subsidiary, announced Wednesday that it had launched a tender offer for KeyHolder, a Tokyo-listed entertainment company with businesses spanning artist management, television and film production, digital content, advertising and logistics.
The offer could give HYBE Japan a controlling stake in KeyHolder, with the maximum investment estimated at 105.7 billion won ($72 million), according to the company's announcement.
KeyHolder owns SKE48's management company through a subsidiary and holds a 50 percent stake in the company operating Nogizaka46 through an affiliated entity.
Nogizaka46, which debuted in 2012, has sold more than 30 million albums and won Japan's Record Awards twice, in 2017 and 2018.
SKE48, formed in Nagoya in 2008, has maintained a strong following, with its latest single, "Tameiki Mirai," selling approximately 335,000 copies in its first week and ranking second on Billboard Japan's weekly singles sales chart.
KeyHolder's roster also includes rock band Novelbright, whose songs "Walking With You" and "Tsukimisou" have accumulated more than 2 billion streams, and actor Hiroshi Tamaki, known for his role as Shinichi Chiaki in the Japanese television drama "Nodame Cantabile."
HYBE Japan plans to combine KeyHolder's artist management experience and established fan base with HYBE's artist development system, global promotional capabilities and Weverse fan platform to develop new artists and expand overseas activities.
HYBE Chief Executive Lee Jae-sang said, "KeyHolder is a proven comprehensive entertainment company with top-tier IP competitiveness and infrastructure in Japan, which is considered one of the world's two largest music markets."
He added, "KeyHolder will serve as a catalyst for implementing HYBE's 'Multi-home, Multi-genre' strategy."
Kim Young-min, chairman of HYBE Japan, said, "I am pleased that leading entertainment companies representing Japan and Korea are joining hands to create productive synergies."
He added, "By combining top-tier Japanese artist IP with HYBE's production system and platform capabilities, we will strengthen our competitiveness in the global music market."
This article was published with the assistance of generative AI and edited by The Korea Times.
